items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: So during this time, as I said, I worked with Sinatra

ctx.x: Well, offstage he would -- you know, we would get -- yeah, we'd still play. But I mean as far as the public is concerned. There were a lot of youngsters who didn't realize what a great pianist Nat was. And I would get him -- sometimes we'd get in these discussions, I'd tell him look, you're foolish. I mean, you want to be a stand up singer like Sinatra. Sinatra wishes he could play piano. I mean, you've got two shots, you've got to let these people know how versatile you are. So he finally started playing, but he…
But as I said, it was up to me to either leave or stay, you know, because I knew what his policy was, I knew what he was driving at, and if I didn't like I should have left. But --
